newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: DECISION NEARS ON CZECH AGROBANKA SELLOFF.
newsitem.headline: DECISION NEARS ON CZECH AGROBANKA SELLOFF.

text.p: Czech Agrobanka a.s. , said on Tuesday its state-appointed administrator would soon choose one of several London-based firms to manage the sale of a majority stake in the bank to a strategic investor.

"Our forced administrator will, within two weeks, choose the best of the bids submitted by several major London investment banks to arrange the Agrobanka's majority stake sale," Agrobanka's spokesman Milan Srb told Reuters.

Srb declined to reveil any further details on the size of the stake or which firms were in contention for arranging the sale, but said the new owner, whether it be foreign or domestic, would be a "strategic" investor.

Agrobanka was put under "temporary" forced administration by the Czech National Bank (CNB) in September after running into liquidity problems stemming from the failure of another Czech bank, Kreditni Banka a.s..
The central bank said Agrobanka suffered a crisis in confidence because of its ties to the Czech Motoinvest investment group which was also connected to Kreditni Banka.
Srb said there would be no certain deadline set for the arranger to sell the stake, though the soonest would be after an extraordinary audit of Agrobanka by Price Waterhouse.
That is expected by the end of December.
"The arranger in cooperation with bank's administrator and shareholders will choose the purchase offer, that would meet conditions set by the administrator," Srb said.
He did not disclose what the conditions would be.
Srb added that the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) had shown an interest in capital involvement in Agrobanka.
Agrobanka is the country's fifth largest bank and the largest fully-private Czech bank.
Agrobanka's forced administration stalled the plans of its Slovak unit to become a fully-independent bank from the beginning of 1997.
